newsitem.title: UK: Sudan accuses U.S., Israel of encouraging attacks.
newsitem.headline: Sudan accuses U.S., Israel of encouraging attacks.

text.p: Sudan's ambassador to Britain on Monday accused the United States and Israel of encouraging neighbouring countries to attack it, but said it was confident of regaining all its lost territory.
Ambassador Yousif Biereedo said at a London news conference that U.S. aid to Uganda, Ethiopia and Eritrea was part of an attempt to crush Sudan's Islamist government.
Israel was implicated by what the ambassador said was its involvement in military training in Eritrea and meetings with Sudanese rebel leaders.
"What is now taking place is the agenda of foreign powers, implemented by neighbouring countries and some of our nationals," Biereedo said.
Sudanese rebel forces say they have seized several towns and 11 garrisons in the Blue Nile area in fighting that started last week.
Sudan admits to losing only the towns of Kurmuk and Queissan and accuses Ethiopia and Eritrea of playing an active role in the fighting. Ethiopia and Eritrea have denied the charges.
Biereedo said some 20 tanks and 6,000 soldiers took part in the incursions in eastern Sudan, using "the tactics of a regular army not a guerrilla war".

"The magnitude of the operation is not available to the guerrilla movement," he said. "The attacks are quite systematic...but we are confident that our armed forces will liberate these two cities very soon."
He said Yemen, Qatar, Jordan and Iraq had all expressed support for Sudan but the Khartoum government was not looking for outside military help.
"We are quite capable of liberating these areas. We are looking for political and moral support at this stage," the ambassador said.
Egypt has refused to intervene, saying the fighting is an internal matter, and President Hosni Mubarak has said he is certain that no foreign troops have entered Sudan.

Biereedo claimed that the United States had adopted a policy since 1995 of seeking to "contain the Islamic government of Sudan", which has been racked by fighting between the mainly Christian south and the Arabised Moslem north since 1983.
He said the United States had sent military advisers to Uganda and that as recently as November 1996 had sent $20 million of military equipment to Uganda, Eritrea and Ethiopia.

The United States, which has put Sudan on its list of countries that sponsor political violence, at the time denied the aid was intended to assist the three countries in a bid to overthrow Sudan's government.
